analysis: The only change in docs/developer/test.md is a documentation edit around line 1049. It updates the SDK 27 release qualification text to SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 (Xcode 27.2) and links the `release` toolchain section of build.md. The supplied units are head-side excerpts at lines 1845-2771, which are unchanged surrounding text and contain no changed lines. I read them for security-relevant content. They describe test procedures: opt-in env gates, task-owned cache roots, `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_*` test settings, owner-only files, and receipts holding counts, timings and hashes only. These describe tests and add no runtime code, keys, endpoints, authorization, attestation or cache-storage behavior. The T-041 prefix-cache defaults (30-minute TTL, HMAC-keyed names, KEK-rooted purge) are not altered by any visible change. The test docs state that persistent caching is disabled only for fixtures, and that `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_PERSISTENT_KEY` must not be `1`, which is consistent with the threat model. No threat assumption is invalidated and no new attack surface is introduced. Remaining question: the toolchain bump is documentation-only here. Any real build-pipeline or toolchain change (for example the `release` toolchain in build.md or CI workflows) lies outside the supplied evidence and would need its own review for T-034/T-013 artifact-integrity implications.
